what: A replay of one Design Studio run: Can we design a bacterium that eats carbon, and could it live anywhere?
live_hint: studio-live.html polls POST /tool/session_read on a running sim-engine/http.mjs and shows that instead when it answers. Start one with: node sim-engine/http.mjs
question: Can we design a bacterium that eats carbon, and could it live anywhere?
verdict: On the designer's own four numbers the strain cannot invade when rare: at the resident guild's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative, so it is excluded. That outcome is a property of those four numbers and not a measurement of anything, and the run says so twice. What the real databases contribute is the other half: where the clade is actually recorded, what is actually in the chosen box, and what is actually recorded as interacting with it -- facts with studies behind them, and no population parameter anywhere among them.

entries.title: Can we design a bacterium that eats carbon, and could it live anywhere?
entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: generation 0: "A bacterium that eats carbon" names no species and no metabolism. Ask for exactly that, and see what the blueprint tool does with a description it cannot read.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: it refuses, and names the words it could not read: bacterium, eats, carbon. None of the three is in the lexicon, so nothing in the description resolved to an organism and there is nothing to build a hierarchy of.

detail.output:
no taxon recognised in "a bacterium that eats carbon and swims".

The lexicon reads a word list, not English, and nothing in this description resolved to an organism.
Words it could not read, any of which might have been the organism: bacterium, eats, carbon

This used to default to Metazoa and build a generic ANIMAL -- organ systems, organs, cell types --
whatever had been asked for. A blueprint of the wrong kingdom is worse than no blueprint.

Either name a taxon the lexicon or organisms/merged/taxa.json knows (a scientific name works:
"Escherichia coli", "Drosophila melanogaster"), add the word to organism-design/lexicon.json under
taxon_words, or ask for the old behaviour explicitly:

  node organism-design/blueprint.mjs "a bacterium that eats carbon and swims" --assume-taxon Metazoa
detail.the_bug_this_replaces: Until this run, that description produced a blueprint of Metazoa -- ALL ANIMALS -- with 8 organ systems, 38 organs and 138 cell types. The taxon silently defaulted to the widest animal clade whenever no taxon word was recognised, on the reasoning that the widest taxon removes no structure by taxon constraint. The reasoning is sound and the behaviour was not: the fallback does not merely relax the constraints, it decides what the organism IS. The word "bacterium" sat in words_not_recognised while the tool built an animal with organs, and nothing connected the two.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: "eats carbon" has at least four readings and they are different organisms: fixing CO2 from the air (autotrophy, which cyanobacteria and plants already do everywhere), oxidising hydrocarbons (Alcanivorax and the oil-degrading guild), depolymerising plastic (Ideonella sakaiensis on PET), or consuming elemental carbon, which essentially nothing does. This run takes the first reading and says so. No layer here disambiguates a request; the words are not read as English, and a tool that silently picked one of four would be guessing in the same way the Metazoa default was.

detail.why: it is the reading with a real industrial chassis to name: Cupriavidus necator fixes CO2 through the Calvin cycle using hydrogen as the electron donor.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: generation 1: Name a real chassis: Cupriavidus necator, which fixes CO2 through the Calvin cycle with hydrogen as the electron donor. It is a bacterium that eats carbon in the first sense and it is already used industrially. Scientific names did not resolve before this run either -- the refusal above advised using one while the reader could not read one -- so this also tests the fix.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: the scientific name resolves (Cupriavidus necator, NCBITaxon_106590) and the hierarchy that comes back is almost empty: 2 organ system(s), 6 organ(s), 1 tissue(s), 1 cell type(s). That is not a failure of the query. Uberon is an ANIMAL anatomy ontology and the Cell Ontology is overwhelmingly animal cell types, so for a prokaryote there is almost nothing in them to find. The anatomical layer of this system has close to nothing to say about most of life, and saying that plainly is better than a thin hierarchy that looks like a result.

conflicts.label: fin
conflicts.axiom: "fin" carries no never_in_taxon axiom that reaches Cupriavidus necator. It was dropped by its in_taxon statements: the ontology asserts it only for taxa that neither contain nor are contained by Cupriavidus necator.

detail.what_this_means: For an animal this layer returns 13 organ systems and several hundred cell types. The same tool, the same queries and the same ontologies return a handful of terms for a bacterium. The layer is not clade-general even though the code is: the DATA stops at the animals.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: the document exists: taxon Cupriavidus necator, placed in Cupriavidus < Burkholderiaceae < Burkholderiales < Betaproteobacteria. The clade table reaches outside the animals as of this run -- it ran from Metazoa downward before, so every bacterium, archaeon, fungus and plant was unplaceable, and unplaceable propagates: no clade scope can be decided, no reference set can say whether it is covered.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: 17 cannot-evaluate, 18 out-of-scope. The law set was written about fish and the scope mechanism now correctly reports that none of it reaches a bacterium, naming the real lineage each time. A law base with nothing to say about most of life is a fact about the law base, not about the bacterium.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: generation 2: The design says "swims". A blueprint cannot answer that: a part list describes one instant and swimming is a cycle. Ask the locomotion layer for the obvious first design -- a paddle that opens and closes, the way anything our size would swim.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: IMPOSSIBLE, by a theorem and not by a simulation: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 9.96e-5 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency. This is the strongest verdict anything in this repository can return short of Lean: not "unlikely", not "inefficient", but zero net displacement per cycle, at any beat frequency, for any organism whose stroke retraces its own path at this Reynolds number. Driving the power stroke faster than the recovery stroke -- the obvious fix, and the one intuition suggests -- changes nothing, because in the Stokes limit the displacement depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate.

detail.theorem: Purcell EM 1977, Life at low Reynolds number, Am J Phys 45(1):3-11
detail.limiting_factor: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 9.96e-5 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency.
detail.what_would_fix_it: break the time-reversal symmetry: a rotating helix, a travelling wave along a flagellum, or a cilium whose recovery stroke follows a different path from its power stroke. Two or more degrees of freedom moved out of phase trace a loop, and a loop encloses area, and enclosed area is displacement.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: generation 3: The theorem names its own escape: break the time-reversal symmetry. A rotating helix traces a loop in configuration space rather than retracing a line, and a loop encloses area, and enclosed area is displacement. That is what a flagellum is. Declare the cycle too, so the arithmetic can be checked against the speed asked for.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: nothing this layer can check contradicts the design. That is NOT a finding that it moves: there is no muscle here, no metabolism, no control and no energy budget, and 1 of the 3 checks are regime indicators that never fail anything.

what_this_is_not: whether the organism can generate the forces its gait requires: there is no muscle model and no actuator model
whether it can pay for the motion: no metabolic rate, no cost of transport, no energy budget
whether it can control the motion or stay the right way up: no stability model
whether the gait is one a nervous system could produce or a developmental program could build

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: generation 4: Every layer so far asked whether the design is internally possible. None of them asked the question that decides whether most organisms exist: is there anywhere it could live that is not already full of something better at living there? Carbon fixation is the most thoroughly occupied trade on the planet.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: GBIF holds 89 occurrence records for Cupriavidus necator A, concentrated in CN, IN, US. In the Rhine-Main agricultural belt, Germany GBIF holds 18 records; the 10 most-recorded non-Aves species are listed. No population parameters were declared, so whether this design could establish against what is there has NOT been evaluated. That question needs numbers no occurrence database contains.

recorded_range.reading: GBIF holds 89 occurrence records for Cupriavidus necator A, concentrated in CN, IN, US.
recorded_range.caveat: Occurrence records are presence and collector effort. They are heavily biased toward wealthy countries, roadsides, protected areas and charismatic taxa. A blank map is a map of where nobody looked as often as it is a map of where the organism is not.

community: Klebsiella michiganensis Saha et al., 2013 (4 records)
Serratia fonticola Gavini et al., 1979 (1 records)
Citrobacter braakii Brenner et al., 1993 (1 records)
Acinetobacter guillouiae Nemec et al., 2010 (1 records)
Klebsiella aerogenes (Hormaeche & Edwards, 1960) Tindall et al., 2017 (1 records)
detail.relationships_note: Grouped from GloBI's own interaction types. 0 taxa recorded eating this clade, 0 recorded parasitising it, 0 in a recorded mutualistic or symbiotic relationship with it, 0 it is recorded hosting. COMPETITION IS NOT AMONG THEM, and that is not an oversight: competition is the one ecological relationship that leaves almost no direct observational trace, because it is two organisms NOT doing something to each other. GloBI records interactions that somebody watched happen. Nobody watches an exclusion. Types this grouping does not recognise, left in "other": hasVector.
cannot_say: whether the design would be outcompeted: that needs growth rates, carrying capacities and competition coefficients, and none of them is in an occurrence record or an interaction record
how abundant anything is: occurrence counts are records, which is sampling effort as much as biology
whether the design could eat what is there, or be eaten by what is there: the interaction records are for its CLADE, and a design is by construction not its clade
anything about the places nobody has surveyed, which is most places
anything about Aves, which is filtered out of every result here by design and is a central part of most terrestrial communities

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: generation 4: The databases hold no population parameter, so the tool will not say whether the design is outcompeted -- it will only say so from numbers somebody declares. Declare them, as the designer's own estimates, and let the criterion run. The answer is then a property of those four numbers and the run says so.

entries.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
entries.body: Against resident soil autotroph guild, the design CANNOT invade when rare: at the resident's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative. It is excluded, on these parameters.

invader K.source: DESIGN INPUT: cells per gram of soil the designed strain is assumed to reach alone. An estimate by the designer, not a measurement; soil carrying capacities for a specific strain are not in GBIF or GloBI and were not looked up.

resident K.source: DESIGN INPUT: the standing community assumed an order of magnitude denser, on the reasoning that it is already there and adapted. An estimate, not a measurement.

alpha, resident on invader.source: DESIGN INPUT: residents assumed to suppress the invader almost as strongly as the invader suppresses itself, because they compete for the same inorganic carbon and the same electron donors.

alpha, invader on resident.source: DESIGN INPUT: the invader assumed to suppress residents weakly, being rare and novel.

detail.model_caveat: Lotka-Volterra two-species competition: phenomenological, no space, no age structure, no environmental variation, no evolution, no third species, and one competition coefficient standing for every way two organisms can get in each other's way. The outcome above is a property of the four numbers that were declared. It is as good as they are and no better, and every one of them is an input to this result rather than an output of it.

generations.asked: Cupriavidus necator that fixes carbon dioxide and swims

genotype.note: Marker gene products the Cell Ontology records for the chosen cell types. For a prokaryote there are essentially no such annotations, which is the same gap as the anatomy: these are animal ontologies.

mesh.why: no surface mesh: the builder is a parametric teleost builder and Blender is absent here. For a rod-shaped bacterium a mesh would be a cylinder, which is a thing a modelling tool can make and not a thing this system knows.

generations.what_it_taught: A scientific name now resolves and the clade table now reaches bacteria, so a prokaryote gets all the way into the studio and the law check. What it finds there is that the anatomy ontologies, the cell ontology and the law set are all animal artefacts. The pipeline is clade-general; its contents are not.

gates_changed: lean_check: not asked -> ran, no opinion

generations.asked: the same organism, swimming with a hinged paddle

body_length_m.source: DESIGN INPUT: a 2 um rod, the order of size Cupriavidus necator is described at. Not a measurement made here.

speed_m_s.source: DESIGN INPUT, swept: 10-50 um/s, the order of speed asked of the design. Not measured on any cell here.

gait.description: a single hinged paddle that opens and closes, driven faster on the power stroke than on the recovery stroke
gait.source: DESIGN INPUT: the first design proposed for this organism

genotype.note: unchanged: this generation changed how the organism moves, not what it is made of. That is the point of a separate locomotion layer.

generations.what_it_taught: IMPOSSIBLE, by a theorem rather than a simulation. At Re of order 1e-5 a time-reversible stroke returns the body exactly where it began, so the paddle design does not move slowly: it does not move. This is a verdict no shape-only layer could ever have reached, because nothing is wrong with the paddle as a structure.

generations.asked: the same organism, swimming with a rotating helical flagellum

speed_m_s.source: DESIGN INPUT, swept: unchanged from generation 2.

gait.description: a rotating helical flagellum driven by a reversible motor: the helix traces a loop in configuration space, not a line retraced

cycle_hz.source: DESIGN INPUT, swept: the rotation rate the design asks of its motor. Not a measurement of any flagellum here.

distance_per_cycle_m.source: DESIGN INPUT, swept: net advance per revolution, a fraction of a body length. Not measured here.

gait.source: DESIGN INPUT: the second design, chosen because the theorem in generation 2 named exactly this escape

generations.what_it_taught: The theorem no longer binds it and the declared cycle is consistent with the declared speed. That is NOT a finding that it swims: there is no motor model, no torque, no energy budget and no control here. It is the absence of a contradiction, which is the most this layer is able to offer.

conflicts.axiom: "fin" carries no never_in_taxon axiom that reaches Cupriavidus necator. It was dropped by its in_taxon statements: the ontology asserts it only for taxa that neither contain nor are contained by Cupriavidus necator.

dropped_from_the_blueprint: queries (13-15 SPARQL bodies with their responses)
genome_sketch markers (kept per generation in gen*.json instead)

honesty.mesh: No generation of this animal has a surface mesh. anatomy-model/parametric is a parametric TELEOST builder and Blender is not installed on the machine this ran on, so no .glb was built and none is shown. The 3D view draws the ONTOLOGY HIERARCHY -- which structures the design has and what contains what -- and that is structure without shape: it cannot be flown, measured for area, or printed.
honesty.declared: The mass, membrane area and airspeed in generations 1-3 are DESIGN INPUTS. Each carries a source string saying so. Nobody has measured a winged mouse and nothing here pretends otherwise.
honesty.verdicts: Every verdict on this page is the string the tool itself returned, with the numbers it returned, copied from the session log. Nothing is recomputed here and nothing is rounded for display except where the page shows a fixed number of decimals.
